themes_detail.label: Dead Animals Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints have spiked to 10 this week—a 344% increase compared to the 2.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.46)—suggesting a potential disease vector or sanitation failure on Upper East Side streets that warrants immediate investigation into root causes.
evidence: 10 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.2 weekly baseline (344% spike, z-score 6.46)
Statistical anomaly indicates acute emerging problem, not seasonal pattern
Public health concern: concentration of dead animals may indicate disease outbreak, pest infestation, or infrastructure failure
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY and NYC Health about whether they've detected a pattern; investigate possible disease vectors or environmental hazard
Canvass affected blocks to identify hotspots and interview residents about what they've observed; check for related pest complaints

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints jumped to 15 this week—a 650% spike versus the 2.0 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 6.5)—indicating either a sudden influx of unlicensed vendors or coordinated enforcement action that deserves scrutiny.
evidence: 15 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly baseline (650% spike, z-score 6.5)
Mobile Food Vendor ranked 6th in spikes by z-score, indicating statistical significance
Vendor Enforcement already a top-10 complaint type (400 total over 90 days), now accelerating
reporting_angles: Contact Department of Health to determine if recent enforcement blitz or street vending licenses triggered complaints; check for pattern by location
Interview Business Improvement Districts or block associations about vendor activity and whether it's linked to recent policy changes

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dogs Dangerous Spike
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints surged to 4 this week—a 967% increase from the 0.4 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 7.49)—suggesting a potential safety hazard or enforcement gap in parks and public spaces.
evidence: 4 unleashed dog complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (967% spike, z-score 7.49)
Unleashed Dog is 4th-ranked spike by z-score, indicating acute emergence
Converges with Animal in a Park spike (9 complaints 3 weeks ago, 227% above baseline), suggesting park safety concern
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about recent enforcement patterns and dog run capacity; identify which parks are hotspots
Speak with dog owners and residents about whether there's a visible enforcement gap or off-leash culture emerging

themes_detail.label: Litter Basket Shortage
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests jumped to 8 this week—a 433% spike versus the 1.5 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 9.19, highest severity)—indicating residents perceive inadequate street sanitation infrastructure.
evidence: 8 litter basket request complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly baseline (433% spike, z-score 9.19—highest ranked spike)
Street Condition is already a top-10 complaint (1,115 over 90 days); litter basket spike suggests infrastructure gap
May be symptom of broader sanitation understaffing or deferred maintenance
reporting_angles: Request DSNY deployment data to verify whether litter baskets are undersupplied on Upper East Side vs. citywide; check installation schedule
Identify which blocks have requested baskets and why; interview DSNY about budget constraints limiting new placements

themes_detail.label: Tree Die-Off Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints spiked to 4 last week—a 1500% increase from the 0.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.66)—possibly signaling disease, pest infestation, or environmental stress affecting Upper East Side street canopy.
evidence: 4 dead/dying tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1500% spike, z-score 8.66—second-ranked spike)
Concentrated emergence suggests localized pathogen, pest (e.g., emerald ash borer), or environmental hazard rather than random tree failure
No recent news coverage detected; early warning signal of potential citywide urban forestry crisis
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks Forestry to investigate whether a specific pest or disease is detected; request tree health data for the district
Visit affected trees to photograph and identify species; interview residents about when they noticed decline
